newsitem.title: CHILE: Bema/Amax Chile Refugio gold mine paralyzed.
newsitem.headline: Bema/Amax Chile Refugio gold mine paralyzed.

text.p: Chile's Refugio gold mine, owned equally by Bema Gold and Amax Gold Inc, has been closed since Saturday because of heavy snowfall at the pit which lies high in the Andes near the border with Argentina.
"Since Saturday, we have not been operating the mine," the pit's human resources manager Anibal Avendano told Reuters by telephone from head office in Copiapo.

Production is likely to resume in two to three days once a new shift of workers arrives to replace the 350 miners who have been stranded in Refugio's base camp after being evacuated from the pit when the weather worsened, he said.
"Buses are leaving (Copiapo) this afternoon with replacement workers. Soon we will be able to start clearing the snow and operations may restart within the next two to three days," said Avendao.
The open-cast pit, which lies a head-spinning 4,700 meters above sea level, is covered by snowfall over two meters deep in places, he said.
Avendao said the company has spent the last three days clearing the road to the base camp which lies 500 meters below the mine.
Refugio, which started operating last year, processes 30,000 tonnes of mineral daily and is designed to produce 230,000 ounces of gold a year when running at full capacity.
Last week's bad weather cut highways throughout northern Chile, including the road to nearby state copper company Codelco's Salvador mine which was damaged by heavy rains and landslides.
